identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Kanaka Durga is worshipped atop Indrakeeladri hill on the bank of the Krishna river at Vijayawada as a swayambhu (self-manifested) form of the goddess. Her four-foot, eight-armed sanctum image is shown standing over the demon Mahishasura and piercing him with her trident, recalling the goddess's victory over him. The temple, officially the Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam, shares the hill with a shrine to Malleswara Swamy, a form of Shiva, and is administered by the Andhra Pradesh Endowments Department.

narrative.summaryIntro:
The Kanaka Durga Temple, officially the Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam, stands atop Indrakeeladri hill on the bank of the Krishna river at Vijayawada, NTR district, Andhra Pradesh. It is dedicated to the goddess Kanaka Durga, worshipped as a swayambhu, eight-armed form of Durga standing over the slain demon Mahishasura, and the hill also carries a shrine to Malleswara Swamy, a form of Shiva.

The temple is administered under the Andhra Pradesh Endowments Department and is among the state's most visited pilgrimage sites, particularly during the Dasara/Navaratri festival, when the goddess is worshipped in ten forms over ten days and large crowds bathe in the Krishna river below the hill.
narrative.documentedHistory:
Popular tradition holds that the sage Indrakila performed penance asking the goddess to reside on his hill and guard the region from demons, and that she went on to slay the demon king Mahishasura, an episode reflected in the sanctum image, which shows her standing over him with her trident. This is presented here as devotional legend rather than documented history.

The earliest datable evidence for worship on the hill is epigraphic: a Telugu inscription of 1229 CE, found in Veligandla village in Prakasam district, records a donation to "the God Bejawada Malleswaradeva at Indrakiladri, known as Dakshina Varanasi," made by Podukayuri Siddayadeva and Sivamagi Maraya for the merit of their chief Siddaraju, alias Trilochana Pallava, described as a Telugu Pallava king. Wikipedia's own account labels this inscription as being "from the Chola era" while also naming a Pallava donor-chief, an inconsistency in the secondary source that is noted here rather than resolved; the inscription itself is significant chiefly for naming the Malleswaradeva (Shiva) shrine at Indrakiladri, indicating worship on the hill was established by the 13th century. The temple states that inscriptions of other, unspecified dynasties are also found at the site, but no further datable detail was available in the sources consulted.

In the modern period, the Devasthanam introduced a Suprabhata Seva for the goddess on 26 November 2018, modelled on the practice at Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams: four priests recite Suprabhata mantras before the sanctum between 3 and 4 AM, with the ticket then priced at Rs 300 and daily participation capped at 25 devotees.

visitingInfo.nearestBusStation: Pandit Nehru Bus Station, Vijayawada (approx. 2 km)
visitingInfo.entryRules: The Devasthanam offers both a free general queue (Dharma Darshanam) and paid faster-access darshan categories, along with sevas such as Archana, Kumkum Puja, Saree Daanam and Annadanam donations, bookable online at kanakadurgamma.org/tms.ap.gov.in or at temple counters. Exact category names, current fees and reporting times were not independently confirmed from an official source that could be fetched directly and should be reconfirmed before travel.
visitingInfo.accessibilityNotes: The Ministry of Tourism's national portal (utsav.gov.in) lists darshan as available daily from 4:04 AM to 11:59 PM; this appears to describe the temple's live/online darshan stream rather than a confirmed physical visiting-hours window, which a separate aggregator source gives with a midday break (see openingHours).
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Devasthana Information Centre: 0866-2423500 / 2423600, toll-free 1800-425-9099; Executive Officer contact eo_vijayawada@yahoo.co.in, Endowments office endow-eosdmsd@gov.in. Address: Indrakeeladri Hill, Brahmin Street, Vijayawada, NTR District, Andhra Pradesh 520001. Confirm darshan and seva timings before travelling, especially around Dasara/Navaratri when arrangements change materially.

shrines.locationDescription: The principal sanctum atop Indrakeeladri hill, housing the swayambhu, four-foot, eight-armed image of Kanaka Durga shown standing over the demon Mahishasura and piercing him with her trident. A Sri Chakram and a Ganapati image are placed beside the main goddess.

Located at the northeast corner of the temple complex. Named in a Telugu inscription of 1229 CE as "Bejawada Malleswaradeva at Indrakiladri," the earliest datable epigraphic reference to worship on the hill.

poojas.description: Arjitha seva introduced on 26 November 2018, modelled on the practice at Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams. Four priests recite Suprabhata mantras before the sanctum; participation was capped at 25 devotees a day and the ticket was priced at Rs 300 at introduction. Current pricing and capacity were not independently reconfirmed.
Food offerings made to the goddess three times a day.

festivals.significance: The temple's principal annual festival. The goddess is worshipped in ten forms across the nine days of Navaratri and Vijayadashami (Swarna Kavachalankrita Durga, Bala Tripurasundari, Annapurna, Gayatri, Lalita Tripura Sundari, Saraswati, Mahalakshmi, Durga, Mahishasura Mardini and Raja Rajeswari Devi), with special alankaram and naivedyam, a Chandi Homam, processions of the utsava murti, and a Teppotsavam (boat festival) on the Krishna river below the hill. It draws pilgrim numbers the district administration treats as of state importance.
Kanaka Durga is worshipped in her Sakambhari (Banashankari) form over three days.
Special Varalakshmi Vratam observed on all Fridays of Sravana month; reported attendance of more than 20,000 devotees during the month.
